verdicts.note: A real chain sprocket with a brass hub and center screw is clearly visible here (chain wraps it); claude's point sits on that hub center, codex wrongly called it occluded.
Optional lower sprocket at the crank axle; claude's point is on the chain-wrapped sprocket between crank-arm and green collar (codex instead mislabeled this same spot as cylinder_gear_center_1).
Codex's point lands on the crank-axle chain SPROCKET, not a uniform-diameter brass cylinder gear; no cylinder gear is separably visible, so claude's occluded call is correct.
Codex's point sits on the body of the CONE gear stack, not a separate cylinder gear; the cylinder gears are occluded behind the cone in this side view, so claude is correct.
Cone side-on, base disc x~765 to apex x~1190; axis midpoint ~x977, and claude's x (982) is nearly exact while codex (1010) is ~33px toward the apex.
Both correctly record the ~20-arm fan as edge-on/unresolvable in the left-side view; no single arm's corners are markable.
Claude sits exactly on the green top-frame casting's top-left outer corner; codex's point is ~135px away out in the black void.
Claude is on the casting's top-right (back) outer corner; codex is ~155px left, sitting on the flat green top face.
Claude is on the base slab's bottom-left outer corner; codex's point is ~250px away up in the black void, not on the slab.
Claude is on the base slab's bottom-right (back) outer corner; codex marked a point on the slab's TOP edge, ~180px up-left of the true bottom corner.
Far (machine-right) side hidden behind the near side; both agree occluded.
Far-side top corner occluded; both agree.
Far-side base corner occluded; both agree.
Far-side base corner occluded; both agree.

summary: Claude was far more accurate on this image, winning every contested feature. On all four visible analyzer corners codex had a large systematic up-and-left offset (~130-250px) that put its points in the black void or on the wrong (top) edge of the base slab, while claude sat squarely on the true corners. Codex also mislabeled two non-cylinder parts as cylinder gears (the crank-axle sprocket and the cone-gear body) and wrongly called the visible pinion sprocket occluded; claude correctly identified the cone gear side-on and both cylinder gears as occluded.
